author: WP12
summary: Updated for the Bible's pin: registration systems, the ContentReader session, type erasure and reader-by-reader wire contracts with evidence. Much of the per-reader validation text is stale at TARGET because the runtime readers now share the canonical decoders: SpriteFont list lengths, exact texture level sizes, Curve counts, SoundEffect loops and index divisibility are checked; Texture2D accepts the whole classic format range and can keep DXT compressed; Texture3D refuses DXT; Model tags are partly accepted; Game registers the built-ins. The site held the reader inventory and registration; the session semantics and per-reader contracts now live on two new deep dives.

concepts.section: XNB Type Readers and Object Graphs
concepts.text: An XNB body is a serialized object graph: its table names reader factories and one ContentReader session constructs the root and nested values, then resolves shared resources.

XNB readers live in the process-wide ContentTypeReaderManager keyed by canonical name; loose and CNJ readers live in per-manager maps keyed by C++ type or CNJ type string; the similarly named extension points are not interchangeable.
tokens: the similar names are not interchangeable

concepts.text: CNA has no reflection fallback for XNB names: every canonical reader name must be registered explicitly, including closed generics and enum readers.
tokens: every canonical reader name must be registered explicitly

concepts.text: Claim that the global registry starts empty and is not populated by Game, so applications must register built-ins before the first load: at the snapshot Game's constructor calls RegisterAllBuiltInXnbReaders; only a standalone manager (tool, test, C API host) must call it.
concepts.note: Bible (updated text) kept the alpha.1 statement; TARGET's Game registers the built-ins.

concepts.text: RegisterAllBuiltInXnbReaders is idempotent because AddTypeCreator ignores a repeat of an exact key.

Claim that closed generic collection readers beyond SpriteFont's dependencies all need exact registration: at the snapshot eleven closed generics are pre-registered by the umbrella call; any further closed combination still needs hand registration because C++ cannot build ListReader<T> by reflection.
tokens: Eleven closed List, Array and Dictionary combinations are pre-registered
concepts.note: Bible listed only the three SpriteFont lists; TARGET pre-registers eleven closed generics.

concepts.text: AddTypeCreator keeps the first factory for an exact key and ignores later ones; ClearTypeCreators clears every family for every manager and exists for test isolation.
tokens: keeps the first factory for an exact key

concepts.text: The XNB registry map is unsynchronised and empty names or empty factories are not rejected (an empty factory fails only when a file names it, with std::bad_function_call); complete registration before concurrent loads.
ReadAsset<T> parses the reader table at the current stream position, reads the shared-resource count, deserialises one indexed root, reads every shared object and then runs the queued typed fixups.
tokens: ReadSharedResources() reads every shared object and only then runs the queued fixups

concepts.text: The constructor comment saying the caller already consumed the reader table is stale; a second ReadAsset does not rewind or reuse the first table, so one reader is one body session.
tokens: so one reader is one body

concepts.text: ContentReader borrows raw pointers to its stream and manager; the manager's own call keeps both alive for the session, and a standalone caller must do the same.
tokens: holds its stream and manager as raw pointers

concepts.text: Initialisation creates one fresh reader per table entry and enforces its serialized-version policy, then calls Initialize in a second pass, matching FNA's two-pass LoadAssetReaders.
tokens: Initialization has two passes, matching FNA

concepts.text: The ContentTypeReaderManager passed to Initialize is a temporary local, so a custom reader must not retain it; the reader instances die with the session.
tokens: The reader instances, the parsed table and the fixup lists die with the session

concepts.text: An unregistered name anywhere in the table fails the whole file, even if no object uses that reader.
tokens: the whole file fails, because the table must resolve in full

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: Object indices are one-based: zero means null and positive n selects table reader n-1; a negative or too-large index is an incorrect type reader index.

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: A zero index returns an existing instance if supplied, otherwise T{} for a default-constructible T; a T with neither raises ContentLoadException because C#'s default(T) has no C++ equivalent.

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: A reader whose result type differs from the requested T surfaces std::bad_any_cast.

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: A positive shared-resource index queues a fixup; all shared objects are read before any fixup runs, enabling forward and cyclic references; out-of-range positive indices are rejected.
tokens: references may point forward and may form cycles

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: Index zero queues nothing, and so does a negative index because the implementation tests only index > 0.
tokens: so a negative index also queues nothing and is not reported

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: Wrong-typed shared values and fixup exceptions are not one transaction: reader-side effects of fixups that already ran survive a later failure.

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: Disposal recording recognises only a statically typed shared_ptr<U> with U deriving from IDisposable and only when a callback was supplied; Load<T> supplies none and untyped reads skip it.

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: ReadAsset<T>'s comment that an empty callback lets the manager record disposables itself does not match the code: ContentReader's manager fallback is still marked deferred.

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: ReadExternalReference<T> returns empty for an empty string, requires a manager, confines the logical path and re-enters Load<T>, walking the full ladder and sharing the typed cache.
tokens: walks the full ladder and shares the typed cache

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: Claim that ReadExternalReference<T> is linked only for Texture2D and TextureCube: at the snapshot it is also instantiated for shared_ptr<Effect> (EffectMaterial's effect reference); other T do not link.
tokens: instantiated for Texture2D, TextureCube and shared_ptr<Effect>
concepts.note: Bible listed two instantiations; TARGET has three.

concepts.section: Indices, shared resources, and external references
concepts.text: The untyped ReadExternalReference() loads only a compiled .xnb through LoadUntypedXnbReference, caches under typeid(std::any) and refuses LZ4.
tokens: insists on a compiled .xnb (no CNB or loose fallback)

concepts.text: XnbReadLimits is applied at named sites, not as one aggregate budget: table and shared counts are checked, collection and decoded-image limits apply when a reader calls their helpers.
tokens: is consulted at named sites, not as one aggregate budget

concepts.text: Typed object dispatch is depth-bounded with an RAII guard that restores the counter after failure; the untyped path (ReadObject(), shared resources, untyped ReadAsset) does not consult it.
tokens: neither checks nor increments that counter
concepts.note: Bible said object dispatch is bounded without qualification; TARGET bounds only the typed path (untyped gap by reading).

concepts.text: The type-reader name bound applies only after the underlying string allocation, and ordinary serialized strings do not use that limit.
tokens: The 1 MiB name limit is applied after the string is read

concepts.text: Because an uncompressed file is read before any compressed-payload control, the limits are defences, not proof that every allocation or object graph is bounded.
tokens: is not refused by the file-size limit at run time

concepts.text: ContentTypeReader<T> lets an author implement Read(ContentReader&, optional<T>); the forced-rename ContentTypeReaderBase erases the call to std::any, and the eventual any_cast is the effective type check because target names are strings.
tokens: the eventual any_cast is the effective type check

concepts.text: Copyable targets are stored directly in std::any and move-only targets boxed as shared_ptr<T>; indexed dispatch unwraps both, which is how bare SoundEffect and move-only roots load.
The direct ReadObject<T>(reader) and ReadRawObject<T>(reader) overloads always cast to bare T and therefore fail for move-only targets; use indexed dispatch.
Claim that TextureCube is a move-only root: at the snapshot TextureCube is copyable (shared renderer); SoundEffect remains the move-only example.
concepts.note: The page names SoundEffect only.

concepts.text: An existing instance is transported into the reader and a value returned; the caller's original C++ object is not updated in place.
Collections differ on existing instances: List appends, Dictionary clears first, Array resizes to the stored count, and the Dictionary<String,Object> reader keeps existing entries.
tokens: keeps an existing map's entries without clearing

concepts.text: Duplicate dictionary keys silently keep their first value because CNA inserts with emplace, whereas FNA's Dictionary.Add throws.

Closed collections create their element readers from the global registry on each read rather than using the initialised peer in the file's table; that suits stateless built-ins, and stateful custom element readers must register and test exact combinations.
tokens: created fresh from the global registry on each read

concepts.text: CanDeserializeIntoExistingObject is declared and overridden to true by ListReader and DictionaryReader but never consulted by ContentReader.
Unless a reader widens SupportsVersion, CNA admits serialized reader version zero only, whereas FNA reads and ignores the version integer; version admission is separate from the container version.
tokens: FNA reads the integer and ignores it

concepts.text: The canonical decoders that read nested objects inline additionally require version 0 of the nested reader, and ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder offers no version setting.
Most runtime readers now share the canonical Decode...XnbData functions with the build-time XNB importer, so one validation governs what loads and what cna-content transcodes.
tokens: One decoder for the game and the build

concepts.text: Primitive readers use explicit little-endian BinaryReader operations, not host-memory layouts: Boolean one byte, integers and IEEE floats their fixed widths.

Claim that XNB Char rejects a four-byte UTF-8 code point: Char decoding belongs to sharp-runtime's BinaryReader::ReadChar, which at the unpinned sibling revision returns the high surrogate and keeps the low one instead of rejecting.
tokens: a four-byte sequence in an XNB Char field is not rejected there
concepts.note: Hedged on the page as sibling-revision behaviour.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime modules/io/src/System/IO/BinaryReader.cpp (ReadChar) at sibling next 41b918c9, not pinned by TARGET

concepts.text: String is a 7-bit byte length followed by bytes stored in std::string without UTF-8 validation.

Math readers are literal field sequences: vectors, quaternion and matrix Singles in public order, Color four RGBA bytes rather than its packed integer, and Plane, Point, Rectangle, box, sphere, frustum and ray from their obvious constituents.
tokens: four bytes R, G, B, A (not its packed integer)

concepts.text: Math readers validate nothing: no finiteness, normalisation, non-negative dimension or radius, min/max ordering or invertibility checks.
Claim that CNA has no generic EnumReader: at the snapshot EnumTypeReader<TEnum> exists, but it is not a built-in and each enum still needs its reader registered (a builder's EnumField does it).
concepts.note: Bible said no enum reader exists; TARGET has an opt-in one.

concepts.text: Evidence for scalar and math layouts is mostly CNA's own writer and reader symmetry; external SpriteFont fixtures exercise only nested Char, Rectangle and Vector3 lists.
tokens: rest on CNA's own writer-and-reader symmetry

concepts.text: Decimal reads the .NET lo, mid, hi, flags wire into mantissa, sign and scale; it is registered only where sharp-runtime reports a native 128-bit integer, so the count is 60 on toolchains without one such as MSVC.
Decimal's reserved flag bits are not validated; the Bible also reports negative zero being canonicalised, which depends on sharp-runtime's Decimal and was not established.
concepts.note: Only the ignored flag bits are stated; the negative-zero claim is not carried.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime BinaryReader::ReadDecimal at an unpinned sibling revision

concepts.text: TimeSpan preserves a signed 64-bit tick count.
DateTime keeps the lower 62 tick bits and drops the two-bit DateTimeKind; a kind value of 3, which the managed constructor rejects, is admitted by the mask.
Tests establish ordinary positive values, not bit-for-bit Decimal or DateTime metadata fidelity across compilers.
CurveReader reads PreLoop, PostLoop, an Int32 key count, then each key's position, value, tangent in, tangent out and continuity; it does not call ComputeTangents.
Claim that a negative key count becomes an empty loop and a large count bypasses the collection ceiling: at the snapshot the count goes through CheckCollectionElementCount, so both are refused.
tokens: so a negative count or one above ten million is refused
concepts.note: Bible described an unbounded count; TARGET bounds it.

concepts.text: Curve enum integers are cast without range checks, NaN, infinity and duplicate positions are admitted, and an existing curve is extended rather than cleared.
tokens: An existing curve is extended, not cleared

concepts.text: Curve evidence is CNA's own curve_two_keys.xnb and focused tests; no externally produced Curve XNB is committed.
Texture2DReader reads surface format, width, height, level count and a byte count plus payload per level.
tokens: a byte count and payload per level

concepts.text: Claim that Texture2D accepts only Color and DXT1/3/5: at the snapshot every XNA 4.0 SurfaceFormat from Color to HdrBlendable plus ColorBgraEXT is accepted, with non-DXT data uploaded as stored and left to device and profile checks.
tokens: every ordinal from Color to HdrBlendable is accepted
concepts.note: Bible listed four formats; TARGET accepts the classic range.

concepts.text: Claim that DXT is always software-decompressed: at the snapshot DXT stays compressed when the renderer reports LoadsCompressedContentNativelyEXT and accepts the block format, otherwise it is decompressed to Color.
concepts.note: Bible said always decompressed.

concepts.text: Under Reach, a block-aligned non-power-of-two DXT atlas is always decompressed to Color because XNA's loader accepted such authored atlases (the Platformer HUD font, DXT3 128x132) though the public Reach constructor refuses that shape.

Width and height must be positive and within the device's maximum dimension; the level count must be level 0 alone or the complete chain; every level's bytes must match exactly and the cumulative decoded size stays within maxDecompressedSize.
tokens: cumulative decoded size of all levels

concepts.text: The device-dimension check was added after the container fuzzer produced real process crashes (Vulkan stack smashing, a non-catchable WebGPU panic) that neither API's validation caught.

Version-4 legacy mapping is narrow: ordinals 1, 28, 30, 32 map to ColorBgraEXT and DXT1/3/5; Claim that the ColorBgraEXT mapping still hits the accepted-format refusal: at the snapshot ColorBgraEXT is accepted for Texture2D.
tokens: of which only four are mapped
concepts.note: Bible said the mapped ColorBgraEXT was then refused; TARGET accepts it.

concepts.text: CNA does not perform FNA's Xbox 360 texture byte swaps at run time; the build-time transcoder refuses Xbox texture payloads instead.
tokens: The payload is not byte-swapped for Xbox 360 files

concepts.text: External-producer Texture2D evidence: a one-pixel MonoGame Color XNB, an LZX 64x64 Color texture (Explosion.xnb), an liblz4-made LZ4 variant, XNA 4.0's Hud.xnb and the DXT3 atlases in two SpriteFonts; no external DXT1/DXT5, version-4 or Xbox Texture2D artifact exists.
tokens: despite its name a 64×64 Color texture
No externally produced DXT1 or DXT5 Texture2D

concepts.text: Texture3D targets a copyable shared_ptr<Texture3D> and stores one blob per level for the whole volume.
tokens: each level is one blob for the whole volume

concepts.text: Claim that Texture3D supports DXT1/3/5 by per-slice decompression: at the snapshot the reader admits only HiDef volume formats (no DXT, no signed normalised) and uploads data as stored.
tokens: DXT and the signed normalised formats are refused
concepts.note: Bible described DXT volumes; TARGET refuses them.

concepts.text: Claim that compressed Texture3D byte counts may carry surplus and no aggregate mip budget exists: at the snapshot every level must be exact and a cumulative decoded-size budget applies.
tokens: every level's byte count must be exact
concepts.note: TARGET tightened the checks.

concepts.text: The Texture3D reader imposes no per-axis limit itself; texture creation refuses volumes on Reach and caps each axis on HiDef with NotSupportedException, which the XNB tier does not wrap.
tokens: The reader itself imposes no per-axis limit

concepts.text: Texture3D evidence is CNA's own texture3d_two_slices.xnb and hand-built bodies whose texture cases skip on renderers that cannot hold textures; no external Texture3D XNB exists.
TextureCube reads format, edge size, level count, then six faces in XNA face order each with all its levels.
tokens: six faces in XNA face order

concepts.text: Claim that compressed cube levels may carry surplus bytes and the face cap is not an aggregate budget: at the snapshot per-level byte counts are exact and the decoded budget is cumulative over all faces and levels.
tokens: cumulative over all six faces and levels
concepts.note: TARGET tightened the checks.

concepts.text: TextureCube still performs no device-dimension query before allocation; DXT stays compressed when the renderer accepts it as a cube block transfer.
A retained MonoGame DXT1 cube travels through ContentManager across six faces and seven levels, sampling selected levels; it does not establish exact pixels, orientation, DXT3/5 or every face.

SpriteFont is a nested graph: Texture2D atlas, glyph and cropping Rectangle lists, Char list, line spacing, float spacing, Vector3 kerning list, optional default character; the umbrella registers the closed list dependencies.
tokens: also registers the three closed list readers

concepts.text: Claim that SpriteFont does not require the parallel lists to have equal lengths: at the snapshot the decoder refuses glyph, cropping, character and kerning lists of different lengths.
tokens: glyph, cropping, character, and kerning counts differ
concepts.note: Bible listed this as unchecked; TARGET checks it.

concepts.text: SpriteFont still does not validate rectangles against the atlas or finite spacing; a duplicate character keeps its last index in the runtime lookup.
tokens: keeps the last index of a repeated character

concepts.text: Reading into an existing SpriteFont throws NotImplementedException, a path ordinary dispatch never reaches.
Two MonoGame fonts (uncompressed DXT3 and LZX) plus XNA 4.0's Hud.xnb establish the ordinary graph and compression, not malformed-font validation.
ModelReader reconstructs declarations, vertex/index buffers, bones, meshes, parts and their shared buffer and effect references; counts and major byte multiplications are bounded.

Vertex-element offsets and enums versus stride, draw ranges and much mesh metadata remain trusted; Claim that index-byte divisibility is trusted: at the snapshot the index byte count must be a whole number of indices.
tokens: The part's draw ranges and much mesh metadata are trusted
concepts.note: Index divisibility is checked at TARGET.

concepts.text: Each bone's serialized parent is read and ignored; parents come from the child lists through AddChild, so contradictory lists leave a bone under the last parent that listed it.
tokens: The serialized parent of each bone is read and ignored

concepts.text: Claim that any non-null Model tag is rejected: at the snapshot the runtime accepts null, Dictionary<String,Object>, Dictionary<String,List<Vector3>> and shared_ptr<System::Object> tags and refuses others; the build-time transcoder refuses every non-null tag.
tokens: a Model with any non-null tag
concepts.note: Bible described the older all-refusing runtime.

concepts.text: Bone references are one byte for fewer than 255 bones and UInt32 otherwise, with 0 meaning none; child, mesh-parent and root references are range-checked; reading into an existing Model throws.

The retained MonoGame cube establishes bones, one mesh and part, buffers, a BasicEffect and fixups, and the container fuzzer mutates it; neither validates arbitrary hierarchy or draw metadata or proves every accepted graph safe to draw.
tokens: None of it proves that every accepted graph is safe to draw

concepts.text: Five readers build BasicEffect, AlphaTestEffect, DualTextureEffect, EnvironmentMapEffect and SkinnedEffect from FNA-shaped fields; they need the device, return shared_ptr<Effect>, and read textures as contained external references.

The general EffectReader reads an Int32 length (at most 64 MiB) and exactly that many bytes of D3D9 Effect Framework bytecode and constructs Effect(device, bytes); without CompiledEffects the failure is wrapped in ContentLoadException; no .fx, HLSL, DXBC or MGFX.
tokens: It accepts no .fx source, HLSL, DXBC or MGFX

concepts.text: Claim listing the compiled-effect renderers as SDL GPU, EasyGL, Software, Vulkan, WebGPU and Direct3D 9/11/12: at the snapshot nine opt-in options (the OpenGL4 one too) plus always-on FNA3D provide the capability.
tokens: nine other renderer families offer it through opt-in build options
concepts.note: Bible's list lacked the OpenGL4 option.

concepts.text: The XnbBuiltInReaders.hpp umbrella comment still calls the general reader a known-unsupported placeholder; the implementation registers the real reader and the known-unsupported hook registers nothing.

Only BasicEffect has external-producer evidence (nested in the MonoGame Model); the other four rest on hand-built field-order tests; reader success does not establish identical draw-time consumption by every renderer.
SoundEffectReader consumes a WAVEFORMATEX block, sample bytes, loop start, loop length and duration; Xbox files get FNA's selective WAVEFORMATEX byte swaps.
tokens: the WAVEFORMATEX fields are byte-swapped as FNA does

concepts.text: PCM16 and PCM8 are taken directly; float and ADPCM are decoded by CNA's own DecodeWavToPcm16; missing MS-ADPCM coefficients are synthesised; XMA2 is rejected.
concepts.note: Bible routed these through SDL's decoder.

concepts.text: Claim that loop metadata is unbounded and an extreme positive pair overflows signed Int32: at the snapshot negative values are refused and loopStart + loopLength is compared with the decoded frame count in 64-bit arithmetic.
tokens: in 64-bit arithmetic, so an extreme pair cannot overflow
concepts.note: TARGET validates the loop region.

concepts.text: The stored duration is a sanity oracle (decoded length more than twice or under half is refused), channels are limited to mono and stereo, and processing caps the rate at 384,000 Hz.
Six external PCM and ADPCM fixtures, a property sweep and move-only root dispatch establish several decode paths, not XMA2, arbitrary extensions or every platform decoder.
tokens: nothing covers XMA2 or arbitrary extensions

concepts.text: RegisterAllBuiltInXnbReaders registers primitives, math, Decimal/DateTime/TimeSpan, Curve, textures, SpriteFont, SoundEffect, Song, Video, stock effects, the general EffectReader, Model support and effect materials.
Claim that Video is registered only when FFmpeg is compiled: at the snapshot VideoReader is registered in every build and reads metadata; playback needs the backend.
concepts.note: Bible kept the FFmpeg condition.

concepts.text: A single unconditional reader count misrepresents builds because Decimal depends on the compiler: 61, or 60 without a native 128-bit integer.
The registration inventory establishes factory presence, not that a companion media file decodes or that playback is linked.
tokens: The count is not a promise about which content loads

concepts.text: A custom binary reader should register the exact canonical name, treat 0 as null and positive indices as one-based, declare a version policy, use indexed dispatch for polymorphic and move-only values, bound counts before allocation, queue fixups, confine external references and keep no references beyond the session.
tokens: Rules for a custom binary reader

concepts.text: A complete reader test includes a real container table, a manager load, nested and shared references where applicable, a failure case before allocation and an observable result beyond construction.
tokens: A complete test uses a real container and table

concepts.text: Summary: CNA implements the XNB object graph without .NET reflection, with explicit boundaries (registered readers, strict versions, finite closed generics, erased move-only representation, reader-specific validation) to be read as scoped contracts rather than one interchangeability claim.

examples.note: The XNB guide carries the same standalone registration example (loading a List<string>); a Game no longer needs the call.

issues.text: Any .xnb whose reader table declares a nonzero version for a built-in reader is rejected; no built-in overrides SupportsVersion, and ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder offers no version hook.
CanDeserializeIntoExistingObject is declared and overridden (ListReader, DictionaryReader) but never consulted by ContentReader.
The object-nesting depth guard covers only typed InnerReadObject<T>; InnerReadObjectAny (Tag values, Dictionary<String,Object> values, shared resources) is unbounded.
ReadAsset<T> doc comment claims the manager records disposables when the callback is empty; the ContentReader fallback is still deferred.
XnbBuiltInReaders.hpp header comment still describes the general EffectReader as a known-unsupported placeholder.
XnbBuiltInReaderRegistrationTests asserting DecimalReader unconditionally: at TARGET the assertion is conditional on SHARP_RUNTIME_HAS_NATIVE_INT128.
No externally produced XNB fixture for Texture3D, Curve, Video, DXT1/DXT5 Texture2D, version-4 textures or four of the five stock effects.
